paragraphs.text: 🐹 Open-source Mac and PC cleaner. Keep your machine clean, light, and running like new. Fast CLI, pl
us native Mac and Windows apps.
macOS · Windows · Linux

Mole
Deep clean, uninstall, optimize, analyze disk and monitor your Mac. Free open-source CLI, plus

a Mac app.
English · 中文 · 繁體 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Deutsch · Français · Polski · Українська · Русский
> 💡 This repo is the free open-source CLI (`mo`). Prefer a native app? Mole for Mac is a separate do
wnload with review-before-delete cleanup, tested leftovers for 800+ apps, maintenance, disk drill-do
wns, live status, and fan controls on supported Macs. On Windows, the native app is Mole for Windows
. `brew install mole` installs the CLI only.
## Features
- **All-in-one CLI toolkit**: Combines CleanMyMac, AppCleaner, DaisyDisk, and iStat Menus style work

flows in one terminal command
- **Deep clean**: Removes caches, logs, leftovers, and orphaned app da

ta to reclaim disk space
- **Smart uninstaller**: Removes apps together with LaunchAgents, preferenc

es, and leftovers
- **Disk analyzer**: Visualizes disk usage with an interactive TUI, finds large fi

les, and navigates directories
- **System maintenance**: Flushes DNS, refreshes QuickLook/icons, and

optimizes system databases
- **Live monitoring**: Shows real-time CPU, memory, disk I/O, network tr
affic, and process stats

## Safety
Mole can remove files, so it validates paths, protects shared and system-owned locations, and asks f
or confirmation when an action needs it. When Mole cannot prove an item is safe to change, it skips
n when an action needs it. When Mole cannot prove an item is safe to change, it skips or refuses it.
- `clean`, `uninstall`, `purge`, `installer`, `slim`, and `remove` can delete files, so review them

with `--dry-run` first and add `--debug` when needed
- Run Mole without `sudo`; it requests administ

rator access only when needed
- `mo uninstall`, `mo analyze`, and `mo slim` route deletions to Trash
by default after confirmation; `clean`, `purge`, and `installer` delete permanently. `mo uninstall

--permanent` skips Trash
- Cleanup activity is recorded in `~/Library/Logs/mole/operations.log`; rev

iew it with `mo history` or disable it with `MO_NO_OPLOG=1`
- Protect caches with `mo clean --whitel

ist`, or maintenance items with `mo optimize --whitelist`
- If the whitelist file cannot be read, `c
lean`, `purge`, and `optimize` stop instead of running without it
Review SECURITY.md and SECURITY_AUDIT.md for reporting guidance, safety boundaries, and current limi

## Configuration
Mole runs without configuration. These environment variables adapt it to slow disks, stalled network
or cloud mounts; raise a timeout only when Mole reports that a step timed out.

- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_QUICK_DETECT_SEC` (2): command-availability probes
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_SHORT_QUERY_SEC`

(3): lightweight queries such as `df` and `tmutil status`
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_MEDIUM_PROBE_SEC` (5): pro

bes that walk a directory tree or reach the network
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_PKG_LIST_SEC` (10): package-mana

ger listings such as `brew list`
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_PKG_CLEANUP_SEC` (20): cache cleanups that walk the

disk
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_DISK_VERIFY_SEC` (30): filesystem verify and repair
- `MOLE_TIMEOUT_HINT_SCAN_

SEC` (15): unbounded user-directory scans
- `MOLE_CLOUD_OFFICE_SECTION_BUDGET_SEC` (300): overall bu
dget for the cloud and Office cleanup section

### Uninstall
`mo uninstall` removes an installed app together with related files that Mole can tie back to that a
pp. It keeps shared data when another installed copy still uses it. If the app is already gone, use
`mo clean` to look for leftovers.
